main_text.p: & Midiã nata est. Lex enim erat: Impietatis conuictus rei capitalis damnetur. Midias Demostheni, curatori ludorum qui in Bacchi dei honorem committebantur, palàm in oculis confpectuque omnium [illegible, ~3 letters] colaphum impegit. ac-cusatur rei capitalis. Intentio Demosthenus: Rei capitalis dānandus es: quippe ἀσελγείας [?] siue ἀσεβείας [?] conuictus. D. Nō sum: sed ὕβρις [?], id est, contumeliae duntaxat. Q. Utrius sit damnandus? R. Quia impietas est, cōtumacia in Deum, iuncta cum contumelia. E-go uerò non Deo, sed Demostheni contumeliam feci. F.

page.notes: The marginal mark on the right beside "in oculis confpectuque omnium" is a small ornamental or non-Latin squiggle (possibly a manicule or a Hebrew/Arabic-looking flourish), not legible as text. Greek words are copied from a small, slightly blurred scan: ἀσελγείας, ἀσεβείας and ὕβρις are marked [?]. "Demostheni" is split across the line break as "Demo" / "stheni" with no printed hyphen, so it is written whole. Possible printing error: "Q. Vtrius" is given as "Utrius" by u/v normalisation, as the Latin text requires.
